topic: Vestigial body parts: palmaris longus, ear muscles, plica semilunaris, tailbone, wisdom teeth
hook: 5 body parts evolution forgot to delete
caption:
Your body still carries parts from ancestors who lived very differently. Some people have a wrist tendon that others simply don't. And the muscles behind your ears still fire when a sound grabs your attention, even though they can no longer move your ears.

Evolution doesn't delete what isn't harmful. It just lets it fade. Part 2 drops tomorrow, so follow @you.didnot.know for one fact a day your body won't believe.

Try the thumb-to-pinky test right now: do you have the tendon? 👇

Evolution doesn't delete what isn't harmful. It just lets it fade. Part 2 drops tomorrow, so follow @you.didnot.know for one fact a day your body won't believe.

Try the thumb-to-pinky test right now: do you have the tendon? 👇

Cover: 5 body parts evolution forgot to delete
📷 unknown (CC0 / public domain) via openverse

1/5 The wrist tendon (15%)
Touch thumb to pinky and flex your wrist. No raised tendon? In many studies, about 15% of people lack it.
🎨 AI-generated image

2/5 Ear muscles
Our ancestors swiveled their ears. A 2020 study found yours still twitch toward sounds, just too weakly to move.
📷 RWhitwam (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

3/5 A third eyelid
The small pink fold in your eye's inner corner is thought to be a leftover of the third eyelid birds still use.
📷 Alpsdake (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

4/5 Your tailbone (Tail)
Every human embryo has a tail for a few weeks. It shrinks before birth, leaving the coccyx at your spine's base.
🎨 AI-generated image

5/5 Wisdom teeth (22%)
Our jaws shrank, so they often don't fit. About 22% of people are missing at least one entirely.
📷 Nizil Shah (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia
